context: Complete prompt-free cross-client Ollama convergence, freshness, restore, uninstall, drift, and operator contracts.
root_causes: The G2 clients did not share a durable marker-owned inventory snapshot.
Background failure states had no exact stale Cloud retention or absolute opt-out contract.
The nominal provider group lacked direct cross-client rollback evidence.
evidence: docs/specifications/ACTIVE/ollama-reverso-provider.md defines the approved G3 scope and ten verification commands.
.ai/work-intake/ollama-reverso-provider-g3-convergence-refresh-docs.md is ready-for-agent and G2 is present in the branch base.
The legacy-safe red command exited 2 on the missing reverso.ollama_convergence freshness and atomicity seam.
solutions: Prepare one marker-owned inventory snapshot and all Ollama client paths in provider-ollama.
Retain only prior marker-owned Cloud rows as stale on bounded background failure.
Make Cloud opt-out local-only and prove background sign-in is unreachable.
Publish isolated verification, operator guidance, fixtures, and drift evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run, apply twice, refresh, and verify are deterministic and prompt-free.
Ollama profile, catalog, launcher, and inventory restore together on handled failure.
Auth-required, timeout, and invalid Cloud results retain only marker-owned stale Cloud rows.
Cloud opt-out invokes neither Cloud discovery nor sign-in.
Unrelated provider hashes and unmarked paths are preserved.
The ten G3 verification commands pass through an isolated wrapper.
legacy_risk_reason: cross-client filesystem atomicity and background authentication boundary
